newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - March 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - March 3.

text.p: Nearly 90 police officers in the past five years have faced in criminal courts charges ranging from indecent assault to sexual violation and incest, according to Police Minister Jack Elder. In written answers to questions asked in Parliament by Labour police spokesman George Hawkins, Elder said that of the 87 officers who faced charges, 46 were still serving with the police. Page 1.

All government MPs would be expected to vote for compulsory supperannuation if it was approved by a referendum, Deputy Prime Minister and NZ First leader Winston Peters said on Sunday. It has been suggested that backbench National MPs might cross the floor to vote against a compulsory scheme if there is a low voter turnout in the September referendum. Page 1.

Several government departments have been told to find further savings for this year's Budget, sources say. Government departments made reports about potential savings to Treasurer Winston Peters early last month. The reports will now be used in Budget planning. Any further funding cuts will be discussed by the Cabinet and Cabinet committees before final decisions are made for the Budget later this year. Page 2.

Fisheries Minister John Luxton is expected to decide on Wednesday to shut down Auckland Islands squid fishing. Squid fishing boats accidentally kill Hooker's sealions, the world's rarest, while they catch squid, and the industry can be shut down when 73 deaths occur. The total is about 70 now. Page 2.

A new Maori television company comprising staff from Aotearoa Television is expected to be announced early this week. Gillian de Beer, spokeswoman for the group, said the National Maori Television Trust had had four trustees -- a prominent figure in Maori television and three Pakeha business people. They were awaiting final details before making an announcement. Page 2.

University staff wanted Education Minister Wyatt Creech to ensure the proposed review of tertiary education fitted the coalition agreement description, their union said last week. The agreement said there would be "a comprehensive review of all aspects of tertiary education", Association of University Staff president Ijan Beveridge said. Page 2.

Associate Health Minister Neil Kirton has come out against last week's decision awarding cardiac surgery in Christchurch to a private consortium, an issue he admits could test the Coalition health policy. The Southern Regional Health Authority had given the contract to the Southern Cardiothoracic Institute, a company jointly owned by Healthcare Otago and surgeons and cardiologists -- some of whom worked for the CHE as well as in private practice, Kirton said. Page 2.

Westpac expects inflation to fall to 1.8 percent at the end of this year, before gradually rising back over two percent. The Reserve Bank is due to issue its March economic projections on March 13. "With inflation expectations which look like remaining over two percent, we do not expect underlying inflation longer term to be at the middle of the band," Westpac says in its latest Weekly Commentary. Page 12.

A call for changes to the closer economic relations rules to ease New Zealand car exports to Australia has been made in a submission to a key advisor to the Australian government on the motor industry. The New Zealand Automotive Component Manufacturers Federation said last week that it had told an Australian automotive inquiry that the CER trade agreement had been particularly beneficial to the Australian automotive industry but of limited benefit to New Zealand. Page 12.

Canada intends to make progress in trade liberalisation and facilitation during its chairmanship of the Asia Pacific Economic Co-operation forum this year, a senior Canadian official says. Canada is this year's host for the various meetings of Apec officials and ministers, culminating in the leaders' meeting in November. Page 12.
